default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-268.title: Tweezer extreme fade
E-268.hypothesis: Two consecutive bars that stop at exactly the same high (low) at the top (bottom) of the recent window show one resting limit order capping two separate pushes; when the second bar closes down in its lower half, the buyers who pushed into it are trapped under an offer that did not move, so fade (mirror at lows).

E-269.title: Scheduled-calm-ahead micro-break fade
E-269.hypothesis: The intraday volatility schedule is very stable across sessions; when the range usually traded over the NEXT minutes at this time of day is well below the range of the minutes just gone (the active window is ending, e.g. after the open or before lunch), no fresh initiators are due, so a 15-minute break made then has nobody to extend it and liquidity providers lean it back; fade it.

E-270.title: Dollar-unbacked VWAP stretch turn fade
E-270.hypothesis: Foreign flow lifts the index and sells the dollar together, so a WIN stretch far above its session VWAP is backed when WDO trades below its own session average; when WIN is stretched above value while WDO still sits above its average, the stretch is local flow, and the first bar closing below the previous low starts the unwind back to value; fade it (mirror below VWAP).

E-271.title: VSA no-demand / no-supply bar fade
E-271.hypothesis: Volume Spread Analysis: an up bar at the top of the recent window on a narrower range than the previous bar and less volume than either of the two previous bars shows professional money is not buying the rise; the push is carried by the last small buyers only, so sell it (no-supply bar at the low: buy).

E-272.title: Counter-VWAP-slope new-extreme fade
E-272.hypothesis: The session VWAP's slope over the window shows where volume-weighted value is migrating; a new window high while value is migrating down means price is probing up on little volume while the volume keeps trading lower; the day's value-setters sell the probe, so fade it (mirror for a new low while value rises).

E-273.title: Scheduled-volatility-ramp break follow
E-273.hypothesis: When the range usually traded over the next minutes at this time of day is much larger than the range just gone (the NYSE open, scheduled US data, the European close), informed participants are about to arrive on schedule; a 15-minute break made as the ramp starts is the first of their orders and the liquidity providers widen instead of leaning, so follow the break.

E-274.title: Candle-open stop-run fade
E-274.hypothesis: Chart traders reset stops and bracket orders at the open of each new 15/30/60-minute candle just beyond the last minutes' extreme; a break printed on the very first bar of a new candle is that one-off burst of reset stops and brackets being triggered, not an initiator, and once it is filled the price reverts; fade breaks made on a candle's first bar.

E-275.title: Seasonal break-outcome fade
E-275.hypothesis: Who dominates each half hour of the session (liquidity providers or breakout traders) repeats from day to day; when over the last 20 sessions the 15-minute breaks made in the trailing half hour of this time of day were, on average, given back within the next minutes, today's break at the same time meets the same providers, so fade it.

E-276.title: Spike-made ceiling break fade
E-276.hypothesis: When most of the window's range was made by one bar, its high (low) is the tip of a single burst that was never accepted: the burst ran into resting orders there and price left at once; a later close through that tip meets the same untouched orders and no accepted value behind it, so fade the break.

E-277.title: Dollar-at-value micro-break fade
E-277.hypothesis: When WDO trades near its own session average price, the dollar is in balance and foreign desks are not repositioning across both markets; with the macro side idle, a short-term WIN break is local flow that index liquidity providers absorb, so fade it (a level-of-the-dollar regime, not its volatility).
